'''Anwar Ali''' (born 1943) is a [[Pakistani people|Pakistani]] physicist and a computer programmer, who served as the Chairman of the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) from 2006 until 2009.{{rp|431}}<ref name="Stanford University Press, Brig-Gen. F. Khan, 2012">{{cite book |last1=Khan |first1=Feroz |title=Eating Grass: The Making of the Pakistani Bomb |date=2012 |publisher=Stanford University Press |location=Stanford, CA, USA |isbn=978-0-8047-8480-1 |pages=400 |edition=1st |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yGgrNAsKZjEC&dq=anwar+ali+long+road&pg=PA431 |accessdate=10 August 2020 |language=en-us |format=googlebooks |chapter={{small|(§ Secret Nuclear R&D Programs)}}}}</ref> His scientific career is spent at the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] as a computational physicist and played a key scientific role his nation's secret [[Pakistan and its Nuclear Deterrent Program|nuclear deterrent program]].<ref name="smuggled" />

==Biography==
===Early life===

Ali, an Indian native from Hoshiarpur, completed his undergraduate studies at the Government College University in Lahore and earned a BSc in physics. He participated in the physics master's program at Punjab University, where he earned a Master of Science (MSc) in the subject. He studied nuclear physics at the University of Birmingham, where he received his MSc.

He was pursuing a doctorate in physics at the University of Birmingham in 1972 when he learnt of India's nuclear test, known as "Smiling Buddha," which took place on 18 May 1974.{{rp|538}}<ref name="Europa Publications, 2007">{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yMc-AQAAIAAJ&q=anwar%20nuclear |title=South Asia |date=2007 |publisher=Europa Publications |isbn=978-1-85743-393-7 |language=en |accessdate=10 August 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Citation
  | last =Abbasi
  | first = Ansar
  | author-link =Ansar Abbasi
  | title = Dr. Ansar Takes Over as PAEC Chief
  | newspaper=The News international
  | date = 3 May 2009
  | url =https://www.thenews.com.pk/
  | accessdate = 6 March 2010}}</ref>

===Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission===
{{Main|Computational physics|Computational fluid dynamics}}
[[File:Computational physics diagram.svg|thumb|left|200px|{{small|A representation of the multidisciplinary nature of computational physics both as an overlap of physics, mathematics, and computer science and as a bridge among them.<ref name=SurveyCompSci>
{{Cite book
| title=A survey of computational physics: introductory computational science
| first1=Rubin H.
| last1=Landau
| first2=Jose
| last2=Paez

| last3=Bordeianu
| year=2011
| publisher=[[Princeton University Press]]
| isbn=9780691131375
| url=http://press.princeton.edu/titles/8704.html
}}
</ref>}}]]

After his graduation from Punjab University, Ali found employment with the [[Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission]] (PAEC) in 1967, as a scientific officer at the Atomic Energy Center in Lahore.<ref name="Paktribute">{{cite news |last1=staff reporter |first1=APP |date=28 March 2006 |title=Anwar Ali, Karim Ahmed appointed new Chairmen of PAEC, KRL respectively |language=en |work=Paktribune |publisher=Pakistan Tribune |agency=Pakistan Tribune |url=http://old.paktribune.com/news/Anwar-Ali-Karim-Ahmed-appointed-new-Chairmen-of-PAEC-KRL-respectively-138804.html |accessdate=10 August 2020}}</ref> He joined the Nuclear Engineering Division alongside [[Sultan Bashiruddin Mahmood|Bashiruddin Mahmood]], an engineer, and aided in the investigations on the uranium enrichment under Bashiruddin Mahmood in May 1974.<ref name="WMD Insight">{{Cite web|title=New Head of Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC) ties with allegedly Nuclear proliferation network |website=WMD Insight |date=28 March 2006 |url=http://www.wmdinsights.com/I5/SA1_NewHeadOfPakistan.htm |format=[[Webcache]] |accessdate=20 March 2010|url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080306150459/http://www.wmdinsights.com/I5/SA1_NewHeadOfPakistan.htm |archivedate=6 March 2008 }}</ref> Ali was an original member of the uranium investigation team,, that was working with Mahmood as a principal investigator, under advice from [[Abdul Qadeer Khan]].<ref name="WMD Insight"/> Ali was posted back to Engineering Division of the PAEC after Abdul Qadeer Khan took over the program after moving it at the [[Khan Research Laboratories]] in Kahuta.<ref name="WMD Insight"/> 
{{Computational physics}}
In 1978, Ali joined the Airport Development Works— a separate facility working on [[electromagnetic separation]] of uranium isotopes. Independent from Khan Research Laboratories— functioning under its director, Dr. [[Ghulam Dastagir Alam|G.D. Alam]], at the [[PAF Base Chaklala|Chaklala Air Force Base]] and assisted Alam in designing of the centrifuge and further in computer programming to control the rotation of the centrifuge.{{rp|57–58}}<ref name="Printwise publications, Rehman, 1999">{{cite book |last1=Rehman |first1=Shahid-Ur |title=Long Road to Chagai |date=1999 |publisher=Shahid-ur-Rehman |location=Printwise publications |isbn=9698500006 |pages=157 |edition=1st |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sNMgAQAAIAAJ&q=Anwar%20Ali%20 |accessdate=10 August 2020 |language=en-us |format=snippet view (google books) |chapter={{small|Gas centrifuge controversy}}}}</ref><ref name="Daily Assas"/> There, Ali learned computer programming from Alam who had also taught him about the [[automatic control]]s after being posted at the Khan Research Laboratories in 1981.{{rp|58–59}}<ref name="Printwise publications, Rehman, 1999"/><ref>Shahidur-Rehman, §PAEC contributions to KRL, pp.144-145, isbn, 9698500006</ref> Eventually, Ali lost interest in nuclear physics but found himself working in computer coding and researching on the topics and applications involving the fluid dynamics in the computational physics.<ref name="Daily Assas"/>

In 1982, Ali was in brief conflict with Abdul Qadeer Khan when he was confided about the latter about selling the centrifuge technology to unknown Arab country, and may have been the one who alerted the [[Zia regime|Zia administration]] to Khan's motive.<ref name="Dawn Newspaper, staff writer, 2004"/>{{rp|contents}}<ref name="Routledge, Kirk, 2017">{{cite book |last1=Kirk |first1=Russell |title=Organizational Cultures and the Management of Nuclear Technology: Political and Military Sociology |date=2017 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-351-50115-6 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JCExDwAAQBAJ&q=Zia |accessdate=10 August 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Daily Assas">Dr. G.D. Alam's interview with Daily Assas, M. Ahmad, 16 December 1998.</ref> Following this incident, Ali was transferred at the Directorate of Industrial Liaison until 1985 when he was posted at the Directorate of Technical Development (DTD) where he found himself working as a computer programmer, and aided in developing computer codes for the launch sequences of the missiles.<ref name=smuggled>{{Citation
 |work=India News Online 
 |title=Pakistan's N-chief smuggled devices from Canada: US report 
 |date=29 May 2006 
 |url=http://news.indiamart.com/news-analysis/pakistan-s-n-chief-s-12503.html 
 |accessdate=20 March 2010
 |url-status=dead 
 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070814025320/http://news.indiamart.com/news-analysis/pakistan-s-n-chief-s-12503.html 
 |archivedate=14 August 2007 
}}
</ref> In 1993, Ali accepted the employment with the [[National Defence Complex]], a rocket engine contractor, and played a key role in designing the satellite-based [[Inertial navigation system|inertial guidance]] and [[control system]] of the [[Shaheen-I]] missile system.<ref>"''New Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission head takes up Post''," Islamabad APP, 5 April 2006; "Former Chairman PAEC Made Secretary Science and Technology," Karachi Dawn (internet version), 7 April 2006; "Anwar Ali Takes over as New Chief of Pakistan’s Atomic Energy Commission," Islamabad The News (internet version), 6 April 2006.</ref> In 1996, Ali went to join the DTD, and helped write the computer codes for the nuclear devices— he was part of the computer programming team that design the codes for the nuclear devices, codenamed: [[Chagai-I]].<ref name=smuggled/>

In 1998, Ali was the Director of the Computation at the Atomic Energy Commission and eye-witnessed the nuclear testing at [[Chagai Hills]], and reportedly quoted: "''Pakistan has successfully detonated the device and we have made a series of experiments and they have been very successful and the results were as we were expecting and in this series there were six experiments.''"<ref name="Associate Press, AP archives, 1998">{{cite news |last1=AP archives |first1=Associate Press |title=Pakistan – Scientists given hero's welcome |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VKLGEP7M4pw  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211220/VKLGEP7M4pw |archive-date=2021-12-20 |url-status=live|accessdate=10 August 2020 |work=Associate Press |agency=Associate Press |publisher=Associate Press, 1998 |date=1 June 1998}}{{cbignore}}</ref> In 1999, Ali was honored with ''[[Hilal-e-Imtiaz]]'' (Trans. Star of Excellence) by the [[President of Pakistan]], and remained associated with his nation's strategic program, namely the Shaheen missile system.<ref name="Paktribute" />

In 2002, Ali was appointed as [[Chief Technical Officer|chief technical officer]] —local corporate designation: Member (Technical)— at the PAEC, and was rumored to become director of the Khan Research Laboratories (KRL), which was rebuffed by the Government in 2004.<ref name="Dawn Newspaper, staff writer, 2004">{{cite news |last1=staff reporter |first1=Dawn newspaper |title=Anwer Ali tipped as next KRL chief |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/353292 |accessdate=10 August 2020 |work=Dawn|location=Pakistan |date=9 March 2004 |language=en}}</ref> Ali, who had been the most senior scientist at the PAEC, was confirmed for the appointment of the chairmanship of the Atomic Energy Commission when the [[Government of Pakistan]] announced at the news media on 28 March 2006.<ref name="Paktribute" /><ref name="Business Recorder, 2006">{{cite news |title=PAEC and KRL get new bosses – Business Recorder |url=https://fp.brecorder.com/2006/03/20060328403450/ |access-date=10 August 2020 |work=fp.brecorder.com |agency=Business Recorder |publisher=Business Recorder |date=28 March 2006}}</ref> Upon taking over the chairmanship, Ali announced that the PAEC has also promoted the utilization of [[nuclear technology|nuclear technologies]] in other areas, such as agricultural production and for medical diagnosis and therapy.<ref name="News International, 2006">{{cite news |title=Anwar Ali takes over as PAEC chief |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/archive/print/642643-anwar-ali-takes-over-as-paec-chief |accessdate=10 August 2020 |work=thenews.com.pk |agency=The News International |publisher=News International, 2006 |date=1 April 2006 |language=en}}</ref> Ali, as chairman of the PAEC, provided strong advocacy for expansion of the commercial nuclear plants to the Government of Pakistan.<ref>{{Cite news
 |last=(PAEC) 
 |first=Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission 
 |title=PAEC undertaking projects for human resource development in high-tech areas: Chairman 
 |publisher=PAEC 
 |year=2007 
 |url=http://www.paec.gov.pk/news-archive-pakatom/na-p-mj07.htm
 |accessdate=20 March 2010
}}{{dead link|date=October 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>"

On 27 January 2006, Anwar Ali, received an invitation letter to visit [[CERN]]– a particle physics facility in Switzerland– where Ali and [[Robert Aymar]] negotiated an agreement between PAEC and CERN to provide financial, technical, and scientific support in the field of novel accelerator, [[collimator]], [[particle detector]] and information technologies, as well as through the training and education of scientists and engineers.<ref name="CERN News, 2006"/> Under this agreement, Pakistan upgraded the [[Compact Muon Solenoid]] and the [[Large Hadron Collider]] by designing and developing the particle accelerators as its lead contractor at the CERN.<ref name="CERN News, 2006">{{cite news|last1=Aymar|first1=Robert|last2=Ali|first2=Anwar|title=Protocol to the co-operation agreement dated 1st November 1994 between the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) and the Government of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan|url=http://clic-meeting.web.cern.ch/clic-meeting/CTF3_Coordination_Mtg/MoU_Addenda/PAEC%20CERN%202006%20P079.pdf|publisher=CERN|date=2006}}</ref>

On 5 April 2009, Ali, rumored to be given extension from his three-year chairmanship, was confirmed for his retirement from the PAEC and was succeeded by Dr. [[Ansar Pervaiz]] on 7 April 2009.<ref name="The Nation, 2009">{{cite news |last1=staff reporter |first1=The Nation |title=Dr Ansar takes over as PAEC Chief |url=https://nation.com.pk/07-Apr-2009/dr-ansar-takes-over-as-paec-chief |accessdate=10 August 2020 |work=The Nation |agency=The Nation |publisher=The Nation |date=7 April 2009 |language=en}}</ref>
